title: Phase 0: Evaluation Harness
goal: Build a reproducible evaluation harness before any serious training work begins.
summary: Phase 0 creates the measurement layer for the lab: task schemas, repeatable suites, backend adapters, Ollama baselines, reports, and reading notes about what makes an eval useful or misleading.

tasks.title: Environment and repo setup
tasks.why: The conda environment, GPU stack, Ollama API, paper library, and git repo give every later experiment a stable base.

tasks.title: Evaluation schema and suite loader
tasks.why: Stable task records make it possible to compare runs without quietly changing what was measured.

tasks.title: Scoring, runner, and reports
tasks.why: The harness needs objective checks, saved records, and human-readable summaries before model comparisons are trustworthy.

tasks.title: Qwen Ollama baselines
tasks.why: Running the same suite against qwen3.6:27b and qwen3.6:35b gives the first real signal that the harness works on local models.

tasks.title: Evaluation reading notes
tasks.why: The papers explain why eval design is as much about failure modes, coverage, and interpretation as it is about scores.

tasks.title: Microlab Console
tasks.why: The dashboard keeps plans, papers, and future eval evidence visible in one place while the project grows.

title: Phase 1: Data and Tokenization
goal: Build the corpus, filtering, splitting, contamination checks, and tokenizer experiments.
summary: This phase turns raw text into controlled training data and makes tokenization choices visible.

title: Phase 2: Tiny GPT Pretraining
goal: Train a tiny decoder-only transformer from scratch and understand every moving part.
summary: This phase favors small models and transparent training loops over raw model quality.

title: Phase 3: Architecture Ablations
goal: Change one architectural decision at a time — norms, positions, MLPs, attention head topology (GQA), and MoE routing — and measure loss, throughput, and behavior.
summary: This phase turns transformer implementation details — including grouped-query attention (GQA) and mixture-of-experts (MoE) routing with load balancing — into concrete tradeoffs.

title: Phase 4: Scaling Experiments
goal: Train a small family of models to see scaling behavior on one GPU, and use muP to transfer tuned hyperparameters across widths.
summary: This phase builds intuition about parameter count, token budget, throughput, bottlenecks, and muP (maximal-update parametrization) hyperparameter transfer, closing with a compute-optimal 1B config.

title: Phase 5: Interpretability
goal: Open up the trained 150M model and find real structure: logit lens, attention patterns, induction heads.
summary: This phase turns 'I built it' into 'I can see what it learned' — decoding every layer's residual stream with the model's own unembedding, scoring induction heads on repeated sequences, and (stretch) watching induction heads form across saved checkpoints. Web reading: Anthropic's In-context Learning and Induction Heads (transformer-circuits.pub).

title: Phase 6: Inference Engineering
goal: Build everything between a checkpoint and a served token: KV cache, sampling, quantization, speculative decoding.
summary: This phase makes inference constraints concrete — why generation is memory-bound, why GQA exists (measure the 4x KV-cache shrink), what int8/int4 cost in perplexity, and how a draft model makes decoding faster for free. The KV-cache exercise is graded by exact token-match against uncached generation. The phase ends by SERVING the model: the authed streaming Playground in the console, backed by the same hand-written KV cache and sampler.

title: Phase 7: Distributed Training
goal: Learn the parallelism vocabulary of every frontier lab — DP/TP/PP, ZeRO, FSDP — and feel it on rented multi-GPU hardware. Ends with the 1B capstone.
summary: This phase hand-writes the per-GPU memory budget, proves it against nvidia-smi on a rented 4x A100 node (~$25-50), measures DDP scaling efficiency on the real 150M training script, and opens with a vendor-affordability research spike that decides whether the 1B capstone trains in the cloud (~12-14h on 8x H100) or locally (~3-4 weeks).

title: Phase 8: Continued Pretraining
goal: Continue training an open base model on a domain corpus and measure adaptation versus forgetting.
summary: This phase connects from-scratch understanding to practical lab workflows.

title: Phase 9: Supervised Fine-Tuning
goal: Create instruction data and train a chat-style model.
summary: This phase focuses on chat templates, instruction data quality, and before/after behavior.

title: Phase 10: Efficient Fine-Tuning
goal: Use LoRA and QLoRA to adapt larger models on the RTX 6000.
summary: This phase makes memory, quantization, adapter rank, and target modules concrete.

title: Phase 11: Preference Data and Reward Models
goal: Build preference pairs, train a reward model, and inspect its failures.
summary: This phase shows where reward modeling helps and where it can mislead.

title: Phase 12: Offline Preference Optimization
goal: Train with DPO-style methods and compare against SFT on the same evals.
summary: This phase studies how preference optimization changes helpfulness, verbosity, and style.

title: Phase 13: RL on Verifiable Tasks
goal: Run reinforcement learning on tasks with automatic, checkable rewards.
summary: This phase builds a verifiable-task environment and studies reward curves, pass rates, and reward hacking on math, code, and schema-validity tasks.

title: Phase 14: Reasoning and Distillation
goal: Generate teacher reasoning traces and distill them into a smaller student, then test whether it actually improves.
summary: This phase explores trace generation, filtering, and distillation, and asks whether the student genuinely gains reasoning ability.

title: Phase 15: Tool Use and Agentic Behavior
goal: Train a model to emit validated tool calls and measure schema validity and task success.
summary: This phase makes structured tool-calling and environment feedback concrete and easy to measure for real behavioral improvement.

title: Phase 16: Final Report
goal: Write a capstone that ties together what improved, what failed, and which methods were worth the complexity.
summary: This phase consolidates the final model card, eval tables, reading notes index, and recommended next experiments.
